name: Beechcraft Duke (60)
summary: Pressurized, turbocharged six-seat piston twin built 1968–1983, sitting between the Baron and the Queen Air in Beechcraft's line.

wings: Low, tapered wing with plain tips
Engines set well out from the fuselage
fuselage: Smooth, rounded pressurized fuselage with small rounded windows
Airstair door at the rear on the left
tail: Swept fin with a conventional low horizontal tail

tellTales: Row of small rounded cabin windows on a smooth, round-section twin
Big three-blade props on large turbocharged engines
Long, smooth nose with a swept fin and plain wingtips

confusedWith.howToTell: The unpressurized Baron has larger windows and is smaller; the pressurized 58P is close, but the Duke is bigger and rounder with a rear airstair door on the left.
The 340 has wingtip tanks on early models, a portly cabin and a swept fin with a dorsal fillet; the Duke has plain wingtips and a smoother fuselage.
The Aerostar has short, narrow wings and large rectangular windows; the Duke has a long tapered wing and small rounded windows.
